label: original-phase input x/m/3/g/t at positions 2-6 after an earlier c/d/k
explanation: Fires almost only during the original (input) phase: 99% of mass, peaking at t=3-4. It never fires at t=0 or on <DEL>, and barely fires in the copy phase. It is token-selective on the current input: x (8x lift), then m, 3, g, t, with weaker s and v. Inputs x/m/3/g alone cover 82% of mass but with precision 0.11, so input identity is not enough. Activation is strongest when c, d or k (and to a lesser degree a, n, f, 0-2) appeared earlier in the prefix. The top examples are all like "c c d x" or "c 0 k x". It mostly fires on the first occurrence of the token. Many trigger tokens that follow a c/d/k prefix still do not fire, so the gating depends on a graded hidden-state context that this predicate captures only partly (dev F1 about 0.39, mass recall 0.65).
